agent.transform.notes: ctx.agent.transform(callback) exists and matches the assumed shape: (callback: (editor: AgentEditor) => void) => Promise<Registration>. callbackRan synchronously (immediately after await)=false. DEVIATION (timing): unlike ctx.command.transform (whose effect was visible via ctx.command.list() immediately after the awaited transform() call), this callback had NOT run synchronously by the time transform()'s Promise resolved. The callback receives a SYNCHRONOUS, in-process AgentEditor (list/get/default/update/remove) — distinct from the async RPC ctx.agent.list().

agent.list.notes: ctx.agent.list() exists as an async RPC call (AgentDomain extends AgentApi = Client["agent"]). DEVIATION: it does NOT resolve a bare array of agents — the resolved value is an envelope { location, data: Array<AgentInfo> }. Observed data.length=7, location field present=true.

catalog.model.list.notes: ctx.catalog.model.list() exists as an async RPC call (CatalogDomain extends CatalogApi = { provider, model: Client["model"] }). Resolves the same { location, data } envelope shape as ctx.agent.list(). Observed data.length=7. DEVIATION (timing): the ctx.catalog.transform(callback) Promise resolved WITHOUT synchronously invoking the callback — callbackRan=false immediately after `await ctx.catalog.transform(...)`. This means the transform callback runs lazily (e.g. on next catalog reload/build), not eagerly on registration, which differs from an assumption that transform() applies the edit immediately.

catalog.model.default.notes: ctx.catalog.model.default() exists as an async RPC call, resolving { location, data: ModelInfo | null }. Observed data=object. DEVIATION (timing): ctx.catalog.transform(callback) resolved WITHOUT synchronously invoking the callback (callbackRan=false), so CatalogEditor.model.default's shape could not be probed at runtime in-line with registration; see the catalog.model.list probe notes for the same timing deviation.

skill.list.notes: ctx.skill.list() exists as an async RPC call (SkillDomain extends SkillApi = Client["skill"]). Same { location, data } envelope shape as agent.list/catalog.model.list. Observed data.length=2.

command.transform.notes: ctx.command.transform(callback) exists. The callback receives a CommandEditor exposing ONLY add(definition) — no list/get/remove on the editor itself; reading commands back requires the RPC ctx.command.list(). Registration returned. Before=2 commands, after transform=3 commands, probe command found=true.

event.subscribe.notes: ctx.event.subscribe(options?: { signal?: AbortSignal, headers? }) exists — DEVIATION: the shape is subscribe(options), NOT subscribe(callback). It returns an AsyncIterable<V2Event> intended for a `for await` loop; there is no Registration/unsubscribe function returned from subscribe() itself (unlike agent/catalog/command/skill .transform(), which all return Promise<Registration>). Cancellation is performed purely by aborting the AbortSignal passed in the options object. Observed: sawAnyEvent=false, loopEndedNormallyAfterAbort=true, terminalError=none.

registration.dispose.notes: Disposed 2 Registration(s) [agent.transform, command.transform]. ctx.command.list() data.length returned to the pre-transform baseline (2), and probe command "weave-feasibility-probe-command" is no longer present (stillPresent=false). Confirms dispose() removes only the proof-owned effect and leaves other registered commands untouched.

create.method: editor.update(id, (agent) => { ...mutate... }) — upsert semantics: when `id` is not already present, update() creates a fresh Agent.Info draft (internally seeded from the @opencode-ai/schema Agent.Info.default(id) helper) and commits it as a new agent on transform flush. There is no dedicated add()/create()/insert()/set() method on AgentEditor.
